## The claim

Direction D3 (BubR1 stabilisation for a hypomorph) has an approved-drug route: a market-approved agent acts on a BubR1-stabilising axis (SIRT2/NAD+ or acetylation) and the axis carries in-vivo evidence of raised BubR1 in a BubR1-insufficient model, i.e. rung 3, possibly through a same-axis proxy compound.

**Prediction if true.** evidence.tsv holds a rung-3 row for the NAD+ repletion axis citing PMID 24825348 (nicotinamide mononucleotide raised BubR1 in vivo in BubR1 hypomorphic mice), and the snapshot returns at least one approved NAD+ precursor or SIRT2-axis molecule (niacin/nicotinamide class) attached to a D3 target.

**What would refute it.** No approved molecule attaches to any D3 target in the snapshot, or the in-vivo BubR1 result cannot be tied to any approved molecule even as a same-axis proxy, leaving D3 at rung 1 or 2 only.

## Evidence

| # | Direction | Strength | Kind | Observation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 111 | supports | 0.60 | literature | The NAD+ precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide raised BubR1 abundance in vivo and SIRT2 overexpression extended median lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice; niacin and nicotinamide, the market-approved and vitamin-form NAD+ precursors, inherit rung 3 on D3 as proxies, both with a US label and a registered study admitting children. | `PMID:24825348` |
| 112 | refutes | 0.40 | absence | The snapshot returned no approved molecule for SIRT2 (10 candidates, unapproved tool compounds plus two drugs with no SIRT2 activation) or for CREBBP, so the prediction that the automated stage would surface an NAD+-axis drug failed; the D3 route exists only because the curated table names it. | `methodology/111` |
| 113 | supports | 0.40 | literature | HDAC2/3 bind and deacetylate BubR1 in mitosis, driving its polyubiquitination and degradation; valproic acid and vorinostat, approved HDAC inhibitors, reach rung 2 on D3 as class-level proxies (no HDAC-inhibitor result on BubR1 levels is cited). | `PMID:28985013` |
